_note: Frozen content for design review. Spinoff of cream-table: every page holds a device frame the user fills with their own screenshot. Rendered here with the slots empty so the placeholder state is what gets judged.
brief: The five screens a one-person business actually runs on

slots.subtitle: Not the stack diagram anyone posts. The five things actually open on the second monitor at four in the afternoon.

slots.toolTagline: One page the whole week points at
slots.bigStatement: Everything lives in one database with three views, because four private lists is how work goes missing.
slots.useNote: Replaced a task app, a wiki and a spreadsheet

slots.toolTagline: The list that decides what ships
slots.bigStatement: If it is not on the board it is not happening, and nothing sits longer than a week without being cut or closed.
slots.useNote: Every item has one owner and one date

slots.toolTagline: The first draft of nearly everything
slots.bigStatement: The blank page is the expensive part. A rough version in thirty seconds changes what you are willing to start.
slots.useNote: Drafting, editing and the reading you skipped

slots.bigStatement: Two people looking at the same frame settle in ten minutes what a thread would not settle in three days.
slots.useNote: Design, decks and anything that needs showing

slots.toolTagline: The only number that is not a vanity metric
slots.bigStatement: Revenue is checked once a day and nothing else is, because the rest moves too slowly to be worth watching.
Five tools is five places to look, and the thing that falls through always falls between them.
slots.useNote: Fewer tools than most, still one too many

slots.body: Everything past the fifth tool earns its place by being opened, not by sounding useful when somebody asks what you run.
slots.signoff: The sixth one is always the one to go
